title: Finite-cover augmentation on every K-injective complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, and $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X_{\mathrm{open}}$ a family with $\bigcup_i U_i=X$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded K-injective complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The actual natural cochain augmentation $\alpha_J:\Gamma(X,J)\to T_U(J)$ defined in [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], using module-valued global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], is a quasi-isomorphism. Neither affine intersections, quasi-coherence, nor injectivity of individual terms of $J$ is assumed.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C1, proof using 01EP and alternating comparison; parent proof Steps 4--5

proof.text: Take a quasi-isomorphism j:J to I with I K-injective and each I^q injective. For each degree q, module injective Cech acyclicity and the ordered-to-alternating comparison imply exactness of the augmented alternating section row of I. In degree zero the sheaf gluing axiom identifies the kernel with sections on X. The tuple-intersection and module comparison defining the actual total identifies these rows with its horizontal rows.

The cone of alpha_I is the total of the augmented rows with columns -1 through r-1, up to the standard cone shift and sign. Every total cocycle is a boundary: choose a horizontal preimage of its highest nonzero column, subtract its total differential, and continue downward. This is legitimate because the horizontal differential of the current top component is zero (the next column is zero), and the exact row supplies a preimage. At column -1 the augmentation is injective, so the remaining component is zero. Only finitely many columns occur, independent of the unbounded vertical degree. This proves alpha_I is a quasi-isomorphism. When r=0 the covering condition implies X is empty, so all sections vanish.

The quasi-isomorphism j between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence by the K-injective comparison theorem. Global sections carries its inverse and both homotopies to inverse maps up to homotopy. The same holds for T_U: for a cochain homotopy h, in the (p,q) summand use (-1)^p times the restriction of h from q to q-1, followed by the corresponding total summand inclusion. The horizontal contributions to dH+Hd cancel because the signs at p and p+1 are opposite; the two vertical contributions give the sectionwise equation dh+hd. The coproduct universal property establishes the total equation. Naturality of alpha gives a square from alpha_J to alpha_I whose vertical maps are thus quasi-isomorphisms. Two-out-of-three proves alpha_J is a quasi-isomorphism.
